implementation_notes: Scala's standard library ships mutable maps, not spatial indexes: the manual realization is a mutable.HashMap[(Int, Int), ListBuffer[Entity]] with getOrElseUpdate as the insert idiom, or a Vector of per-cell buffers for bounded worlds (scala-lang API). Tuple keys are convenient but allocate on every lookup, so packed Long keys are worth the trouble on hot paths. The hand grid remains the default; JTS STRtree (a Java library usable from Scala) fits only build-once geometry workloads.
pitfalls: mutable.HashMap is not thread-safe; an actor or confined simulation thread is the usual fix rather than locking the grid.
Tuple keys box and allocate; specialized structures or a Long-packed key keep the inner loop allocation-free.
ListBuffer appends are amortized O(1) but removal is linear scan; a mutable.LinkedHashSet is the better cell container when entities move out often.
